options.content:
The experience is classified into three levels based on user performance metrics:

Good: Optimal web page performance with fast load times and smooth user interaction.
Average: Acceptable performance with minor delays or issues that do not significantly impact user experience.
Frustrating: Poor performance with slow load times or errors, likely causing user frustration.

parameters.name: cmdb_ci_business_app
parameters.title: Used with the 'State' field on Linux and Windows Servers

options.content:
GSK Observability Platform
Application: slims4
← Back to Site Detail

slims4 Availability
Availability is calculated using two independent methods:
  • Real-time Monitoring
    • A TCP probe is sent to https://app.myslims4.com every 2 minutes.
    • A successful probe indicates the service is available; a failed probe indicates it is unavailable.
  • Outage Records
    • Availability is calculated based on recorded service outages.
To ensure accuracy, the dashboard displays the lower of the monitoring-based availability and outage-based availability calculations.

spec.rawSql:
WITH outage_rows AS (
 SELECT DISTINCT
   outage_begin,
   outage_number,
   site_code,
   application_name,
   outage_duration_minutes
 FROM public.v_incident_site_app_by_app_service
 WHERE outage_number IS NOT NULL
   AND (business_app = 'S239580144')
   AND $__timeFilter(outage_begin)
),
total_outage AS (
 SELECT
   COALESCE(SUM(outage_duration_minutes), 0) AS outage_minutes
 FROM outage_rows
),
total_window AS (
 SELECT
   EXTRACT(
     EPOCH FROM (
       $__timeTo()::timestamptz
       - $__timeFrom()::timestamptz
     )
   ) / 60.0 AS total_minutes
)
SELECT
 ROUND(
   (
     (tw.total_minutes - ot.outage_minutes)
     / tw.total_minutes
   ) * 100.0,
   2
 ) AS availability
FROM total_outage ot
CROSS JOIN total_window tw;

WITH time_buckets AS (
  SELECT
    generate_series(
      date_trunc('hour', $__timeFrom()::timestamptz),
      date_trunc('hour', $__timeTo()::timestamptz),
      interval '1 hour'
    ) AS time
),

base AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    site_code,
    application_name
  FROM public.site_application_services
  WHERE (business_app = 'S239580144')
),

outage_rows AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    outage_begin,
    outage_number,
    site_code,
    application_name,
    outage_duration_minutes
  FROM public.v_incident_site_app_by_app_service
  WHERE outage_number IS NOT NULL
    AND (business_app = 'S239580144')
    AND $__timeFilter(outage_begin)
),

hourly_outages AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('hour', outage_begin) AS time,
    SUM(outage_duration_minutes) AS outage_minutes
  FROM outage_rows
  GROUP BY 1
)

SELECT
  tb.time,
  ROUND(
    (
      (60.0 - COALESCE(ho.outage_minutes, 0))
      / 60.0
    ) * 100.0,
    2
  ) AS "Availability"
FROM time_buckets tb
LEFT JOIN hourly_outages ho
  ON ho.time = tb.time
ORDER BY tb.time;
